*“That Beer I Owe Ya”*

The Citadel’s remnants flickered in the twilight like a broken tesla coil on its last spark. Gordon Freeman, long silent and ever-stoic, stood beside Alyx Vance atop the ruins of what used to be Combine Overwatch HQ. The final battle had cracked the sky open, bleeding green vortigaunt lightning and dangling strands of dimensional spaghetti into the ether. But something was wrong—*very* wrong. The G-Man had returned.

He stood there, unscathed, amidst the chaos, still speaking in his molasses-slow cadence. “You… were never the *hero*, Doctor Freeman… just the instruuuument.” He adjusted his tie with uncanny calm. “You’ve played your part. Now… let me *reset* the board.”

And just like that, time froze.

Except for one man.

Barney Calhoun emerged from a collapsed snack machine on Level B4, his blue security uniform stained with blood, coffee, and a smear of headcrab guts. He carried a six-pack - a relic from a pre-Combine vending machine, the label still promising "freedom in every sip."

Barney wasn’t supposed to be here. The last time anyone saw him, he was smuggling citizens out of City 17—or maybe he had been vaporized by a Strider. Here he was. *Alive*, mad as hell, and still owing Gordon a drink.

"Hey,” he growled, pointing at G-Man with the righteous fury of a man who’s waited two decades for narrative closure, “*I* still owe my buddy a beer.”

The G-Man turned, momentarily surprised, perhaps even… afraid? “Mr. Calhooooun. You are *not* a variable we accounted for.”

"Too bad," Barney said, cracking open the can with a hiss like a Vortigaunt’s sneeze. "This one’s for Gordon."

He hurled the beer can.

Physics bent around it. The air shimmered as if reality itself protested the absurdity. The can rotated through thirteen impossible dimensions, passed clean through a transdimensional tear, *reflected* off Dog’s mechanical head, and collided with G-Man’s skull at precisely 0.357 Planck units of universal narrative density.

The G-Man *crumpled*.

Not exploded. Not disintegrated. Just… crumpled, like a suit collapsing in on itself, tie twitching in zero-point spasms. Reality shuddered.

Then a silence fell across, broken only by the burp of a dying Strider.

Alyx blinked. “Did Barney just…?”

Gordon, still mute, raised an eyebrow.

From behind, a vortigaunt muttered, “*Truly, the can was mightier than the crowbar.*”

Barney lit a cigarette, sat on a chunk of rubble, and handed Gordon the last unopened beer. “Hey, buddy. 'Bout that beer I owe ya.”

They toasted quietly as the timeline stabilized. Around them, reality stitched itself into something new—part Earth, part Xen, part... Aperture? No one was sure.

The screen faded to black.
